title: Heuristic-driven stream reassembly for interleaved toolcall metadata and truncated JSON fragments
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Customers increasingly use the Redwood streaming API with interleaved tool/function calls. We see two recurring failure modes: 1) tool metadata interleaves with JSON output from the model (e.g., a tool call emits non-JSON lines or debug prefixes), and 2) the model or network truncates output mid-JSON object. Existing resumable/retry heuristics are brittle: they either reject partially valid fragments or retry in ways that produce duplicate toolcalls.

Goal: Implement a heuristic-driven reassembly layer in the gateway runtime that: (a) recognizes mixed streams where toolcall markers and JSON tokens interleave, (b) reconstructs a best-effort JSON object from fragmented tokens using sentinel heuristics, escape normalization, and soft-repair rules, and (c) provides idempotent retry semantics for tool/function calls to avoid duplicate side effects.

Scope: Focus on streaming text paths (hosted API + Dedicated gateway). Do not change model-side generation logic. Add opt-in compatibility flag in requests (structured_reassembly=aligned) initially behind feature flag.

Non-goals: Full semantic repair of arbitrarily corrupted JSON, automatic invocation of human review, or altering downstream tool runtimes to be idempotent (we will prefer gateway-side idempotency wrappers).

Acceptance criteria:
- New runtime component passes unit/integration tests for at least five synthetic failure scenarios (interleaved tool tokens, mid-string truncation, nested JSON cut at escape boundary, unicode multi-byte truncation, and mixed-ldjson where a record breaks across frames).
- Gateway exposes a deterministic reassembly decision in response metadata (reassembly_status: passed|repaired|unrecoverable) and a short repair_summary string.
- When repair yields a valid JSON object and a toolcall boundary was present, the gateway routes the single reconstructed object to downstream handlers and ensures the toolcall executes exactly once via an idempotency token/handshake.
- Performance: p99 additional latency for reassembly must be <5ms for <2KB fragments and <20ms for <32KB fragments in our staging hardware.
- Backcompat: Default behavior unchanged; feature disabled unless request opts in or customer is on Dedicated with opt-in console toggle.

Implementation notes:
- Input model stream is tokenized into framing units by existing stream parser. Add a lightweight heuristic layer between framing and structured-parser.
- Heuristic rules (ordered):
  1) Detect explicit tool markers (e.g., "[TOOL_START] toolName", existing toolcall seals) and treat those as boundary anchors.
  2) Normalize common debug prefixes ("DEBUG:", "LOG:") by stripping if they precede JSON braces on the same frame.
  3) Use bracket/balance counters for { } [ ] at byte-level, but respect UTF-8 codepoint boundaries to avoid splitting multi-byte chars.
  4) If truncated string escape is detected (ends in backslash or incomplete \u hex), attempt safe closure by adding the minimal escape completion (e.g., append \uFFFD or closing quote) and mark as repaired.
  5) If multiple JSON fragments separated by tool metadata are detected, attempt to emit each reconstructed JSON object in order, associating toolcall metadata to the closest following object unless explicit toolcall separator indicates otherwise.
- Idempotency for toolcalls: implement a gateway-side client-idempotency token that is created when the gateway detects a toolcall in the stream. On retries due to network or resumptions, the gateway will supply the same token and the tool runtime must be able to dedupe based on token. Add fallback: if downstream tool reports "unknown-token" or no dedupe support, gateway will buffer tool invocation until it can confirm single execution via a lightweight handshake (ack or read-only probe). Document behavior in SDK.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for each heuristic rule with golden inputs/outputs.
- Integration tests using our stream-simulator harness (refer to test-suite streaming-reassembly) that replay recorded customer failure traces (sanitized) and fuzzed truncation scenarios.
- Load tests on staging with a synthetic workload that injects 10% of streams with fragmentation; measure latency, memory overhead, and correctness.

Monitoring and observability:
- Emit reassembly events to the tracing system with tags: reassembly_status, repair_reason, bytes_repaired, toolcall_detected, idempotency_token_used.
- Dashboard: streaming-reassembly (counts, p95 latency, repair_rate, unrecoverable_rate) and alert if unrecoverable_rate > 0.5% over 1h for production.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1: Feature flag behind runtime flag on staging; run tests + internal smoke. (1 week)
- Phase 2: Enable for Dedicated customers who opt-in via console toggle; monitor for 2 weeks. (2 weeks)
- Phase 3: Gradual rollout to hosted customers as opt-in param in API (after docs and SDK updates). (4 weeks)

Docs/SDK changes:
- Add docs page: "Streaming structured reassembly" describing opt-in, trade-offs, and examples of repaired payloads.
- SDK: include a flag in streaming client builders to set structured_reassembly behavior and surface repair_summary in response metadata.

Security considerations:
- Repair heuristics must not mask exfiltration or malicious payloads. For customers with strict compliance, we will provide an "audit-only" mode that logs repairs but refuses to repair automatically.
- Flag security_review_required for broader rollout.

Dependencies:
- ENG-90312 (stream parser refactor) [in progress]
- ENG-89100 (toolcall idempotency handshake) [blocked on runtime API]
